title: SSOT adoption sweep: skills, README, and docs cite @-addresses instead of copying item text
description:
Epic 2821e177 made project knowledge addressable (`@/<kind>/<self-id>` over invariants, rules, gates, requirements, definitions), but the surrounding tooling still copies prose: skills paste invariant/rule text into dispatch prompts and review protocols, and README/docs restate registry content. Copied text re-creates the drift problem the epic solved. Sweep the authored surfaces to cite addresses and resolve them on demand, per the principle recorded in `dev/studies/addressing-v2-item-use-cases.md` §3: write the fact once in the registry or issue section that owns it; everywhere else, cite the address.

## Operating rule: three tiers by read heat

Classify every occurrence of registry-owned text (invariant/rule/gate/requirement/definition content) on a swept surface into one tier; the tier decides the edit:

1. **Projection (hot path, loaded every session).** Text machine-rendered from a registry (the CLAUDE.md invariant region, `docs/reference/rules-and-gates.md`) stays inline: it is a renderer-owned copy, safe by construction. Leave it alone, and never hand-cite where a projection already inlines the text.
2. **Gloss + address (warm prose where readability matters).** README, docs narrative, and skill explanations keep a clause-length paraphrase followed by the address: "append an event per state change (`@/invariant/event-log`)". The address is authoritative; the gloss is a hint and stays short enough that drift is harmless.
3. **Bare address + resolve (behavioral text agents act on).** Dispatch prompts, review protocols, and gate-semantics passages in lead skills cite the address without paraphrasing behavior. Each dispatch-prompt template carries one standing instruction — cited `@/…` addresses are resolvable context; resolve them via `jit item show` before acting on them (chained calls in one shell invocation resolve several at once) — rather than a per-citation instruction. Lead review protocols verify cited addresses resolve.

Decision rule per occurrence: rendered from a registry -> tier 1, leave as is. An agent will act on the text -> tier 3, replace the paraphrase with the address. Otherwise explanatory -> tier 2, gloss + address. Skill-owned rules (e.g. lead-invariant sections) are the skill's own content, not registry items, and stay as prose.

## Folded scope: invariant id uniformity

Invariant self-ids are the outlier among project-scoped kinds: rules and gates use lowercase-kebab self-ids and let the address's kind segment carry the kind (`@/rule/label-format`, `@/gate/cargo-ci`), while invariants double-encode it in all-caps (`@/invariant/INV-LABEL-FORMAT`). Before the sweep cites invariant addresses, rename every invariant self-id to the uniform form: strip the `INV-` prefix and lower-case the remainder (`INV-LABEL-FORMAT` -> `label-format`, `INV-DAG-ACYCLIC` -> `dag-acyclic`, and so on for all eight). Same-named items of different kinds (`@/invariant/label-format` vs `@/rule/label-format`) are distinct addresses by construction.

The rename lands in: `.jit/invariants.toml` ids; `[item_kinds.invariant].id-pattern` (to `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, matching rule and gate) and the `namespaces.enforces` examples, in both the repo config and the `jit init` scaffold (`crates/jit/src/hierarchy_templates.rs`); the re-rendered CLAUDE.md invariant region (`jit invariant render`); Rust comments and doc-comment examples that cite `INV-…` ids. Code-comment citations use the `@/inv/…` alias form (see Sequencing); doc-comment example ids in `cli.rs`, `domain/item.rs`, and `validation/projection.rs` switch to the lowercase convention. Historical documents (`dev/archive/`, `dev/sessions/`, CHANGELOG) keep their original wording.

## Surfaces

1. Repo-tracked skills under `.claude/skills/` (jit-manage, jit-breakdown, jit-parallel, jit-execution-lead, jit-planning-lead, jit-project-lead and their references/): apply the tier rule. Restatements of invariant/rule/gate behavior become tier-3 citations (`@/inv/event-log`, `@/rule/coverage-preview`, `@/gate/code-review`); explanatory mentions become tier-2 gloss + address. Dispatch-prompt templates gain the standing resolve instruction; lead review protocols verify cited addresses resolve.
2. `README.md` and `docs/`: introduce the addressing scheme and `jit item` as the way to cite project knowledge; every place quoting an invariant/rule/gate definition carries its address (tier 2). `docs/reference/rules-and-gates.md` is the rendered SSOT example to point at (tier 1).
3. `CLAUDE.md`: guidance outside the rendered invariant region cites addresses rather than restating rule/gate behavior.
4. Conventions: document the `enforces:@/rule/…` / `enforces:@/gate/…` / `enforces:@/invariant/…` label convention for work that changes enforcement mechanisms.

## Sequencing

A tier-3 citation must never resolve to less information than the prose it replaces. Rule descriptions (`8d2c5ff3`, a dependency of this issue) enrich `jit item show @/rule/…` and the rendered reference; the skill sweep lands after it so resolved text carries the behavioral detail the removed prose held.

Address shorthand: a config-declared kind-alias feature (a sibling task, dependency of this issue) lets `[item_kinds.invariant]` declare `aliases = ["inv"]`, so `@/inv/<self-id>` resolves wherever a kind is named. Canonical rendered output stays `@/invariant/<self-id>`; the alias is the citation form for agent-facing authored text — skill files, CLAUDE.md guidance, and Rust code comments. README and docs cite the canonical form, since they introduce the scheme to readers. The rename and sweep land after the alias task so `@/inv/…` citations resolve.

User-global skill copies under `~/.claude/skills/` are outside this repository; this task updates repo-tracked surfaces and notes the sync expectation in the README section it adds.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: every repo-tracked skill file that restates invariant/rule/gate content is converted per the tier rule — behavioral text to bare address (tier 3), explanatory text to clause-length gloss + address (tier 2) — and each dispatch-prompt template carries the standing resolve instruction; invariant citations in skill files use the `@/inv/…` alias form; a sweep table (file -> tier -> change) is linked to this issue via `jit doc add` as evidence.
- [hard] REQ-02: README and docs/ introduce the addressing scheme and the cite-the-address convention; quoted registry content carries its address; renderer-owned projections stay inline and are identified as such.
- [hard] REQ-03: CLAUDE.md guidance cites addresses for rule/gate/invariant references outside the rendered invariant region; invariant citations use the `@/inv/…` alias form.
- [hard] REQ-04: every `@/…` address cited by the swept surfaces (skills, README, docs, CLAUDE.md, Rust comments) resolves via `jit item show` (dangling-citation check attached as evidence); `jit validate` stays green.
- [hard] REQ-05: every invariant self-id is lowercase-kebab without a kind prefix, uniform with rule and gate self-ids: the registry, the config id-pattern, the `jit init` scaffold, and the rendered CLAUDE.md region all agree; `jit item show @/invariant/<id>` resolves all eight renamed ids; `jit invariant check` stays green; no `INV-`-prefixed invariant id remains outside historical documents.
- [hard] REQ-06: Rust comments and doc-comment examples cite invariants by address in the `@/inv/<self-id>` alias form, and doc-comment example ids follow the lowercase convention; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` stay clean.
